topic.title: The referral that becomes a debt
topic.claim: A referral isn't a favour, it's a loan, and we spend more energy fearing the repayment than weighing the offer.
topic.behaviour: People hesitate to take a better job because someone referred them elsewhere. Others refer a partner or friend to their own company and then carry the outcome, good or bad, as their own.
topic.mechanism: Referrals turn a hiring decision into a social relationship. Saying no or failing feels like letting a person down, not just losing a job. That puts guilt and belonging ahead of the career maths.
topic.group: young professionals in tech and corporate jobs
real_details: One poster felt worse about the new offer because a referral had got them in the door
Another poster referred a spouse to their new company, and she went through two technical rounds
The rejection feedback arrived by HR message and landed hard
The couple's pay gap, around 3 LPA versus more than double that, made the pressure personal
Salaries at the small startup were reportedly delayed by two months
topic.why_now: Switching season means a lot of people are deciding whose name they're carrying into a new office.

score.reason: fresh framing of referral-guilt, strong send-to and group
score.best_hook: A referral isn't a favour. It's a loan you're terrified to default on.
